title: Choose the visual world
question: Choose a visual system for the complete E-Gatepass experience. Existing student, administrator, guard, analytics, and scanner workflows remain unchanged.

options.label: Campus thresholds
options.lineage: University campus architecture and its directional-sign systems
options.thesis: Every request is a clear passage from intent to an authorized campus exit.
options.viewport: A student workspace with role navigation, a focused request form, and a three-stop request-to-gate route showing its current status.
options.risk: The route could compete with dense admin work unless it stays quiet outside status moments.

options.label: The academic timetable
options.lineage: Printed university timetables and academic calendars
options.thesis: Time is the spine: every departure request reads as a dated event with a clear next state.
options.viewport: A time-first application beside a dated request timeline; admin review and guard verification reuse the same chronology.
options.risk: A timetable can overemphasize dates and feel too dense on a phone.

options.label: The campus exit board
options.lineage: Boarding documents paired with live departure boards
options.thesis: A gate-ready request stays in view as its decision changes.
options.viewport: The student sees a gate-ready request beside its approval state; guard actions retain the pass identity.
options.case: The held-in-place status change clarifies the review-to-gate handoff, while travel cues are less specific to a campus.
options.risk: Too literal a boarding-pass treatment could suggest airline features the product does not provide.

options.label: Campus route notation
options.thesis: A single marked path makes each request's next step obvious.
options.viewport: Role-specific work areas follow the request route, with its active step marked and labeled in text.
options.case: Campus wayfinding fits the student's setting; the route must describe workflow and not invent a geographic map.
options.risk: A geographic interpretation could imply location features that do not exist.

options.label: Disciplined information grid
options.thesis: A precise module grid puts dense request information into a predictable scan order.
options.viewport: A clearly labeled request list with predictable columns and actions, becoming roomy rows on mobile.
options.case: The grid discipline transfers, but crowded modules weaken the confirmed priority of mobile ease.
options.kept: A strict scanning order for dense administrative information.
options.risk: Compact modules would work against the confirmed mobile-usability priority.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional administration dashboard with neutral surfaces, summary tiles, and a familiar request table.
canonCard.viewport: A neutral shell, summary tiles, and a table of requests with approve and reject actions.
canonCard.risk: Clear but interchangeable with other admin dashboards.
